note: The paper's own numbering is broken: the ordinary-versus-electric-car chapter is printed as '2' a second time, and two headings that context_extract.py picked up ('2 D(CV)' on p7, '56 Critical Point:' on p17, '5 Power sector to xc 10' on p15) are axis or table text, not headings; those regions are filed under the real heading above them. 'Tbl.' labels are invisible to context_extract.py, so Tbl. 1 to Tbl. 7 were read from the page text by hand. Five unlabelled 'Notations' blocks are ruled two-column tables and are counted as tables, which is why this paper has fifteen tables against seven printed table numbers.
rules: Exhibit labels are the bare strings 'Fig. N' and 'Tbl. N' with no caption body, so every caption is a two-word text-layer label and the tables keep the same form [caption.verbatim].
The paper abbreviates Table as 'Tbl.'; the numbering field uses the closest closed-enum member, 'Table N.', and the verbatim keeps the abbreviation [caption.numbering].
Every label in this paper is set below its exhibit, so position is below for figures and tables alike [caption.position].

Family follows the ink rather than the label: p5 r2 is a perspective wireframe surface and p7 r1, p11 r2, p12 r1, p13's curve and p17 r2 are connected series, so they are recorded as surface-or-3D and line respectively [geometry.family].
p5 r2 has a receding depth axis and a mesh drawn in perspective, so the three_d field is surface-mesh rather than a flat two-axis plot [geometry.three_d].
The p8 r2 demand chart is an embedded bitmap with a printed source url and the p13 r2 network picture is a bitmap too, so both are photo-or-raster-image [geometry.family].
p11 r1 draws discrete real-data points under a fitted curve, so it is scatter while its neighbour p11 r2 is line [geometry.family].
Four exhibits are grouped columns over named categories with the series named only in a key: p15 r2, p16 r1, p17 r1 and p18 r2, so they are bar [geometry.family].
The Fig. 15 exhibit is three pie charts with one shared key; the vocabulary has no pie class, so it is recorded as other with an explicit other_note and panel_count 3 [geometry.panel_count].

Key placement is read off each frame: most figures box their key inside, the p17 r1 legend sits outside at the right because fourteen series will not fit, and single-series p17 r2 has no key at all [geometry.legend].

Four regions on p19 are the individual pies and the swatch legend of the Fig. 15 composite, measured again inside its bbox; they are excluded as fragments, not counted as extra figures [place.page_order].
Every measured block in this paper is a fully ruled grid with vertical rules between the columns, so rule_style is vertical-rules throughout [table.rule_style].
No table shades alternate rows, so zebra is false everywhere [table.zebra].
Tbl. 7 merges the type cell over each pair of constraint rows, so merged_cells is true for that table only [table.merged_cells].
The appendix table on p22 repeats its year header three times as the block runs across the page, so header_rows is 3 there [table.header_rows].
Only Tbl. 1, Tbl. 4 and the p22 appendix blocks print units in the header cells; the rest leave the unit in the prose [table.units_in_header].
Only Tbl. 6 is referred to in the body text ('listed in Tbl. 6' on p16); every other table is named only by its own printed label, so those mention blocks are the null form [mention.lead_pattern].
Fig. 12 has no in-body reference anywhere, only the printed label, so its mention block is the null form while the label still supplies the caption [mention.first_page].

Two exhibits are split across a page break: Tbl. 6 starts at the foot of p14 and continues on p15, and the notation block runs from p9 r2 to p10 r1; both halves are counted as tables and marked continued [table.continued].

Section paths follow the printed heading the region actually sits under: Fig. 3 is above the '6. Computation of Electricity Margin' heading on p7 so it belongs to section 5, and the p19 pies sit above the Conclusion heading so they stay in the EV sensitivity section [place.section_path].
